idiom_name: Encodable view-context struct + Leaf/Vapor view renderer (HTML) or Content (JSON)
implementation_notes: Stage one is a struct conforming to Encodable holding the logical page - Vapor's Leaf guide prefers exactly that over a [String: Any] dictionary because the context must be an Encodable value - so the page is typed, testable and reusable. Stage two is the renderer: req.view.render("invoice", vm) runs the Leaf template for the HTML channel, while the same struct can be returned directly as Content/Codable for a JSON route; Leaf tags (#(variable), #for, #if) carry all channel formatting and never touch the struct. Keep HTML out of the struct and treat templates and the context type as a versioned pair; choose server-side rendering like this when one logical page must also feed e-mail or an API, and Leaf's layout tags (#extend/#export/#import) when the HTML channel needs shared furniture.
pitfalls: Leaf resolves context fields by name at render time, so renaming a Swift property breaks the template only when that channel is exercised - templating errors here are runtime, not compile-time.
#unsafeHTML bypasses Leaf's escaping for trusted fragments; user data inside it is an XSS hole, and a fragment escaped for HTML is wrong for the JSON channel.
The view renderer needs the Leaf provider registered on the Application and must not block the NIO event loop; heavy work belongs before the render call, not inside it.
